## CodeQL engines

> **Last verified:** 2026-10-22 — eleven engines at 2.27.3 from one `mkEngine`
> factory, the local query client and optional per-database daemon, plus the MIT
> Nix extractor at 0.3.0; the javascript engine wraps its launcher with a Node;
> named lifecycle tasks publish atomic checkout generations from shared warmed
> merge-base snapshots, with locked space management and exact stamped worktree
> references. Packs and `customizePackage`: customize.md.

### What a bundle is

GitHub ships the CodeQL CLI as three things in one directory, `codeql/`:

- the **engine**: the `codeql` launcher, the evaluator's jars and a bundled JRE
  (`tools/linux64/java/`), plus `.codeqlmanifest.json`, which tells the launcher
  where extractors and packs live;
- one **extractor** directory per language (`javascript/`, `cpp/`, ...), each
  with its `codeql-extractor.yml`;
- **query packs** under `qlpacks/`: the standard libraries and queries.

A per-language bundle carries that language's extractor and packs plus those it
depends on (the actions bundle also carries javascript). The full bundle carries
every language. The bare CLI zip carries every extractor and no packs.

### The eleven engines

`ai.devTools.codeql.codeql-<engine>`, flat name `codeql-<engine>`:

| engine       | asset                                  | repository                   |
| ------------ | -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| `bare`       | `codeql-linux64.zip`                   | `github/codeql-cli-binaries` |
| `full`       | `codeql-bundle-linux64.tar.zst`        | `github/codeql-action`       |
| one language | `codeql-bundle-<lang>-linux64.tar.zst` | `github/codeql-action`       |

The languages are actions, cpp, csharp, go, java, javascript, python, ruby and
rust. All are x86_64-linux only (each recipe directory has a `platforms.nix`, so
the attribute is absent on Darwin). Each installs to `$out/share/codeql` with
`bin/codeql` symlinked to the launcher, which resolves its distribution by
following the symlink. The javascript engine's `bin/codeql` is instead a
`makeWrapper` of the launcher that sets `SEMMLE_TYPESCRIPT_NODE_RUNTIME` to its
`nodejs` argument (`passthru.nodejs`, swapped with
`.override { nodejs = ...; }`): the TypeScript extractor runs Node, and the
bundle ships none.

The leaf name repeats `codeql` because a flat package name is the last key of
its path (`lib/facets.nix` `flattenPackages`): `ai.devTools.codeql.javascript`
would publish a flat package called `javascript`. The `codeql` namespace keeps
the engines together under `ai.devTools`, and the prefix keeps every flat name
unique and matched by the `codeql` push filter.

`autoPatchelfIgnoreMissingDeps` lists the JREs' X11, font and sound libraries
and the .NET runtime's LTTng provider. The list was measured over every x86-64
ELF in the full bundle and the bare zip, which contain the same 123 objects;
everything else they need is glibc, libstdc++, libgcc_s, zlib or the bundle's
own libraries. It covers build-time linking only. What an extractor needs at run
time (a Python, a .NET ICU) is for the PR that wires that extractor.

### Licence position

Unfree under the GitHub CodeQL Terms, which forbid sharing, publishing or
distributing the CLI, and allow automated database creation only for an
OSI-licensed codebase hosted and maintained on GitHub.com.

So no engine may reach the public Cachix cache. Three guards, all aimed at
public publication:

- `pushFilter: kiro-cli|codeql` on every credentialed cachix-action step;
- `dev/scripts/ci-packages.py` excludes every `codeql-` name from the package
  shards, by prefix, so a new engine is excluded without an edit;
- the `test` job's tripwire asks the cache for every engine and every source
  asset and fails unless each answers 404
  (`dev/scripts/assert-not-published.sh`).

The tripwire excludes the local MIT `codeql-query` client from its `codeql-*`
roots: it has no separate source asset. Engines and the extractor retain their
two-derivations-per-root check, and the separate Kimchi database and
customized-engine checks remain required.

The private Hestia check cache in this repository's GitHub Actions cache MAY
hold an engine: a check builds one, and that is CI-internal storage, not
distribution. Only public publication is forbidden. The public `packages` output
omits the engines because they are unfree.

### Updates

One update target, `codeql-full`. Every engine carries the same
`passthru.updateScript`, a `mkUpdateScript` whose `platforms` are keyed by
engine, so one run moves the version and all eleven hashes together. The version
is the newest `codeql-bundle-v<x.y.z>` tag on `github/codeql-action`
(`git ls-remote`). `releases/latest` is wrong there: codeql-action's own `v4.x`
and `v3.x` releases interleave with the bundle tags.

### CI cost

CI builds ONE engine. `codeql-javascript-smoke` builds javascript and runs
`codeql version` (must equal the pinned version) and `codeql resolve languages`
(must list javascript). `codeql-engines-eval` evaluates every engine's drvPath
without building, and requires the flat `codeql-*` names to equal the
`sources.json` entries.

Building all eleven fetches 2.2 GB and unpacks and patches 5 GB, and none of it
is ever cached publicly, so every run would pay it again. Since the eleven
differ only in the asset, building one proves the shared body and evaluating all
proves every call site and pin.

The update pipeline's input lanes skip the engines for the same reason:
`verify_all_packages` builds every other `ciPackages` entry through
`ci-packages.py update-plan`, which drops the `codeql-` prefix from both the
expected set and the `--select`. An update PR still runs the smoke check in
`ci.yml`.

### External Nix extractor

`ai.devTools.codeql.codeql-extractor-nix` installs the prebuilt MIT v0.3.0
extractor through fetchurl and autoPatchelf, alongside the same tag's
`jamiemagee/nix-all` QL library. `extractor-sources.json` pins both assets; its
separate update target moves them together. No Rust build is involved. The
package's `codeqlLibraries.nix` names its library for `customizePackage`. All
existing public-cache guards stay in place; their `codeql` name filters
conservatively cover this package too. It carries no CLI.

`codeql-extractor-nix.codeql` exposes one javascript engine customized with this
extractor (`engine`), a `mkQueryPack` spec (`queries`), and `createDatabase`,
the script used by `codeql:nix:up`. A javascript bundle supplies CodeQL's util
and yaml packs, which the Nix library imports. `searchPath` discovers the
extractor; `additional-packs` cannot do that.

### Local database lifecycle

`dev/codeql-databases.json` declares each database's name, source kind, CodeQL
passthru, and creator program. `dev/tasks/codeql.nix` generates three explicit
tasks per name plus shared space-management tasks, using one lifecycle
implementation:

```bash
devenv tasks run codeql:nix:up       # create only when source/tool inputs changed
devenv tasks run codeql:nix:refresh  # force a new generation
devenv tasks run codeql:nix:down     # remove this checkout's publication/generation
devenv tasks run codeql:gc           # prune unused shared bases and orphan generations
devenv tasks run codeql:status       # show generations, stamp ages, allocated bytes and references
```

`<checkout>/.devenv/state/codeql/<name>/db` links to a complete generation.
Creation finishes before an atomic link rename publishes it; the previous
generation is deleted afterwards. `stamp` and `engine` resolve through the same
link to that generation's one-line input record and query engine. Each
generation's engine link is an indirect Nix GC root, registered before
extraction and removed with that generation on failure, retirement or `down`.
Treat source and extracted relations as immutable; CodeQL may write its query
result cache. Resolve the link for each request, and serialize queries on one
generation: CodeQL's cache has an exclusive lock. A reader already holding the
previous generation can be interrupted by its retirement, so finish it before
refreshing. Legacy real-directory databases must be moved aside before `up`; the
lifecycle refuses to replace them or delete a foreign symlink target.

The Nix source is committed repository content. For each checkout, the shared
base is `git archive $(git merge-base HEAD origin/main)`, under
`$(git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir)/codeql/nix/`. Its key
includes that commit, engine, creator, standing query pack, descriptor and
lifecycle implementation. A lock builds and warms it once, then `cp -a` copies
it to checkout generations. Hardlinks would let query and overlay writes corrupt
the base. The standing pack is `nix-agentic-tools/nix-queries`. Overlay-capable
extractors warm it with
`database run-queries --cache-at-frontier --no-use-precompiled` and retain
overlay caches with `database cleanup --cache-cleanup=overlay`. Ordinary
fallback databases use `database run-queries --no-cache-at-frontier` and
`database cleanup --cache-cleanup=trim` (CLI 2.27.3). Warming and cleanup set
`--max-disk-cache=512` in MB. Before publication, each generation runs
`database cleanup --cache-cleanup=fit --max-disk-cache=512`: keep useful cached
results within the limit. This bounds intermediate query results, not database
relations or source archives; future queries need the same evaluator cap.

The actual extractor's `codeql-extractor.yml` selects the source behavior. If it
declares `overlay_support_version`, every refresh copies the pristine warmed
base and overlays the entire working diff against its commit, including deleted
and untracked `.nix` files. The stamp hashes those files' contents; overlays are
never chained. The current v0.3.0 extractor has no such declaration: changes to
HEAD rebuild from `git archive HEAD`, while HEAD equal to the base reuses its
warm copy. Dirty edits are excluded in this fallback and do not invalidate its
stamp. A moved merge-base or tool path does invalidate it. Shared bases survive
`down` for other worktrees to reuse.

Every successful `up` (including a matching stamp) and `refresh` prunes, as does
`codeql:gc`. The checkout builder lock protects generation deletion; only
unpublished `generation.*` directories at least five minutes old are orphans.
The current generation is preserved regardless of age, and replacement still
retires the previous generation immediately. Shared-base pruning takes the same
`base.lock` as creation and copying, always inside the checkout lock, without
locking other checkouts. It reads `git worktree list --porcelain -z`, ignores
missing directories and recomputes each live checkout's merge-base. Each
checkout's published stamp supplies the tools, descriptor and lifecycle hash for
its exact current base key; the current invocation's used key is preserved too.
Missing, legacy or malformed stamps do not retain caches. Unborn checkouts and
unrelated histories have no current base and are skipped; a missing
`origin/main` or another Git failure remains an error. Unreferenced bases and
interrupted `base.*` staging directories are deleted under `base.lock`. Deleting
a cache can require a later rebuild; published generations hold independent
copies. No Nix evaluation is needed for `gc` or `status`.

`status` prints one line per declared checkout database (name, generation, stamp
age and allocated size), one per shared base (key, allocated size and worktree
references), then checkout, shared and combined byte totals. Sizes include
retained orphans and query output in the checkout state, without following the
engine's Nix store link. Shared totals cover the declared databases in this
clone's common Git directory.

The local-only `codeql-refresh` entry in `config/repo-validation.nix` uses the
existing prek installer and `hooks:isolate-config` mechanism. After a merge or
branch checkout it detaches a refresh of databases already up in the checkout,
logging to each database's `refresh.log`; a file checkout does nothing. It reads
the checkout's current lifecycle code and descriptor, including after a pull.
The launcher keeps hook failures advisory even on a branch without the lifecycle
script; explicit tasks still report failures. It never creates an inactive
database, waits for extraction in Git, or changes `core.hooksPath`. No database
task runs on shell entry. A fetch, commit or dirty edit needs an explicit `up`
to check freshness.

`codeql-lifecycle` fixture-tests stamps, committed snapshots, shared base reuse,
independent copy inodes, cumulative overlays, publication and failure retention,
forced refresh, registered engine root lifetime, down, detached hook selection
and launcher failure handling without real CodeQL. It also covers current, young
and orphan generations; live and missing worktree references; stale stamps after
merge-base changes; exact tool-version retention; inactive, unborn and unrelated
worktrees; Git error propagation; interrupted-base cleanup; current-run base
protection; builder/shared lock ordering; and status byte totals.

`codeql-nix-strict-header` compiles the shipped Nix query pack, resolves the
external language through merged and nested config files, checks conflicting
search paths are refused, and runs `StrictHeader.ql` over fixtures. It checks
`writeShellScript`, `writeShellScriptBin` and `writeShellApplication` for the
full strict header, including the application's `bashOptions` and the shopt in
`text`. Rows classify text as `ok`, `missing` or `unknown`; local lexical
bindings, concatenation and interpolation are followed, while an opaque helper
call remains unknown. This is a textual AST query, not Nix or Bash execution.
The whole repository is deliberately not a gate.

### Query client and optional daemon

`ai.devTools.codeql.codeql-query` ships
`codeql-query run <name-or-db-path> <query.ql>` and
`codeql-query run <name-or-db-path> -e '<QL text>'`. A name resolves from the
current checkout upward to `.devenv/state/codeql/<name>/db`; a path may name
that database or its containing state directory. Resolve `db` once, then use
that generation's sibling `engine/bin/codeql` to select its exact engine. Files
keep their sibling imports and manifest. Inline queries use a persistent
content-addressed pack whose dependencies are the database languages' visible
`*-all` libraries; ambiguous libraries require a query file in an explicit pack.
Both the manifest and query are published atomically so concurrent first-use
clients see complete files. Output is `bqrs decode --format=json --sort-key=0`
JSON; `--sort-key` accepts other comma-separated column indexes. Compilation
failures print CodeQL's diagnostic, including the query's path and line.

`ai.codeql.queryDaemon.enable = true` is the only daemon switch, off by default
and available on Home Manager and devenv. It declares
`ai.codeql.services.codeql-query`, lowered by `ai.services` to a user unit or
devenv process; normal service controls start and stop it. The socket is
`query.sock` under the service runtime directory,
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/ai-service-codeql-query` or
`${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ai-service-<uid>-codeql-query`, and is claimed through the
owner's path group. The daemon makes that directory private and locks it before
removing a stale socket. Clients use this socket automatically; an absent or
refused socket runs `codeql query run` and the same JSON decoder. Other socket
or query errors fail visibly. `--no-daemon` explicitly selects the fallback and
requires the database to be unlocked. Shutdown interrupts incomplete socket
reads before joining handlers, then releases evaluator sessions and removes the
socket; complete queries finish normally.

The daemon starts one `execute query-server2` lazily per resolved database and
engine, with a separate request lock per database. Different databases can run
concurrently. Aliases of the same target reuse one process.
`resolve ram --ram=6000 --format=json` supplies the server's heap and off-heap
flags; `--threads=4` bounds evaluation. A server releases its registration and
exits after 300 idle seconds. The daemon's `common-caches` persists under
`$XDG_STATE_HOME/codeql-query` (Home Manager) or `$DEVENV_STATE/codeql-query`
(devenv); the fallback's is under `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/codeql-query`. Each database
also keeps CodeQL's own writable evaluator cache.

Every request resolves the live `db` symlink again. A changed generation
detaches the previous registration and reuses or registers the new target; a
once-per-second idle sweep also releases generations whose links changed without
another request. An in-flight query uses the generation it resolved and can be
interrupted by lifecycle retirement; finish queries before refreshing. Plain
database directories remain supported, but must not be mutated while registered.
Database creation, frontier warming, copying, refresh and generation retirement
belong to `codeql:<name>:up|refresh|down`; `codeql-query run` only queries. The
query daemon never changes source snapshots or rebuilds a database.

`codeql-query` is the tiny-fixture integration check: fallback and socket JSON
agree; A/B/A requests preserve results and affinity; concurrent requests, inline
and edited queries, compile-error recovery, generation replacement, unlocked old
generations, idle exit and shutdown with incomplete clients are exercised
against the pinned engine. A lightweight transport regression pauses first-use
writes to each inline file while a second fallback caller compiles, and checks
SIGTERM with accepted idle and partial clients. The transport uses the 2.27.3
`vscode-codeql` `messages.ts` and `run-queries.ts` protocol:
`evaluation/registerDatabases`, `evaluation/deregisterDatabases` and
`evaluation/runQuery` with Content-Length framing. No initialization request is
required.

## CodeQL packs and customizePackage

> **Last verified:** 2026-10-22 — `ai.devTools.codeql` carries `mkQueryPack` and
> `mkModelPack`, which return pack specs; every engine's `customizePackage`
> realizes them; packs reach CodeQL through a generated `CODEQL_CONFIG_FILE`;
> query packs are precompiled; the wrapper execs codeql over a merged config
> named by its content, reused only when no other line sets its options.
>
> **Settled — do not relitigate.** Each was measured on the 2.27.3 javascript
> bundle and rejected:
>
> - **A symlink farm of the distribution with the packs inside it.** The
>   launcher accepts a farm, but the manifest globs do not descend a symlinked
>   directory (`codeql/javascript-queries` stopped resolving), a symlinked pack
>   root resolves zero queries, and a pack without a lock file in the
>   distribution root fails dependency resolution. A sibling of the distribution
>   is searched only one level deep and only in real directories.
> - **`--search-path` for the packs.** It survives a command-line
>   `--additional-packs`, but `--model-packs` finds extension packs only through
>   `--additional-packs`.
> - **Engine passthru builders:** a stopgap for the overlay forcing #2810 fixed.
> - **A child codeql with a trap that deletes the merged config.** The 2.27.3
>   launcher runs java in the foreground and traps only EXIT, INT and TERM, so a
>   HUP left the JVM running on a deleted config, and the wrapper cannot reach
>   the JVM to forward signals; the wrapper execs over a file named by its
>   content instead (`git show 80d4c57a`).

### Surface

```nix
codeql = ai.devTools.codeql;
codeql.codeql-javascript.customizePackage {
  queries = [ (codeql.mkQueryPack { name = "me/my-queries"; src = ./ql; }) ./plain-dir ];
  models = [ (codeql.mkModelPack { name = "me/my-models"; src = ./models; }) ];
  extraPackages = [ pkgs.gnumake ];
  searchPath = [ codeql.codeql-extractor-nix ];
}
codeql.codeql-javascript.override { nodejs = pkgs.nodejs-slim; }
```

`mkQueryPack` and `mkModelPack` return a pack spec, plain data
(`_type = "codeql-pack-spec"`, `kind`, `name`, `src`), and read no engine
(`lib/specs.nix`). The flake's `lib.ai.devTools.codeql` exports the same two
functions for a caller without the overlay.

A spec is not a derivation until an engine realizes it, because a query pack
compiles against one engine's bundled `codeql/<language>-all`: the same spec
realized by two engines is two packs. A builder that returned a derivation would
pick an engine before the consumer named one, so the namespace could not offer
it beside the eleven engines. `customizePackage` realizes each spec against the
engine it is called on (`lib/packs.nix`). A model pack's content is only its
language's, so two engines that carry it realize one derivation.

A language bundle supplies the default language, and a spec's `language`, when
given, must name a bundled or external library. `codeql-full` needs `language`
on the spec and throws naming the field without it; `codeql-bare` has no bundled
libraries and throws unless an external library is supplied through
`searchPath`. Every field is optional, and a bad argument throws. `queries` and
`models` take a directory holding a qlpack.yml, a pack derivation or a spec of
that field's kind. `customizePackage` on a customized package appends. A store
path given twice, in one call or across calls, is used once, and two realized
specs with one pack name throw. A plain directory's pack name is not checked at
eval time; CodeQL reports a pack found in two locations when the packs are used.

The result has `bin/codeql`, a wrapper of the engine's, and `share/codeql`, a
link to the engine's. Nothing of the distribution is copied. Its `unwrapped` is
the engine, and its `packs` holds the realized `queries` and `models`.

### How packs become visible

The wrapper sets `CODEQL_CONFIG_FILE` to a store file:

```text
--additional-packs <every pack>:<the aggregate model pack>
--model-packs nix-agentic-tools/customized-models
--search-path <external extractor/library paths>
```

Only options with entries are emitted. `searchPath` takes package derivations or
directory paths; package `codeqlLibraries` maps external language names to
library pack names. For example, a query spec with `language = "nix"` depends on
`jamiemagee/nix-all` when `codeql-extractor-nix` is in `searchPath`. The same
search path reaches precompilation; raw external libraries are staged with
writable modes because CodeQL rewrites their copied manifests. Customizing the
result appends search paths too, and a subsequent query sees earlier external
libraries.

CodeQL reads that file in every subcommand, including the ones it starts itself.
Measured:

- The form is `--option value`. `--option=value` is ignored without an error.
- Each option keeps one value: a second line replaces the first, and the same
  option on the command line replaces the file's. A consumer who passes
  `--additional-packs` or `--model-packs` on the command line replaces these
  packs for that call.
- A model pack applies only when `--model-packs` names it, and a config line
  names one. So the wrapper builds one aggregate pack holding every model's data
  extensions, each under its index with its own `dataExtensions` globs, and
  `extensionTargets` merged. The copies drop their qlpack.yml, so each model
  pack resolves by its own name once.
- `CODEQL_CONFIG_FILE` replaces CodeQL's per-user `~/.config/codeql/config`. It
  does not add to it.

### A consumer's own config file is merged

The consumer's file is `CODEQL_CONFIG_FILE` when set, else
`~/.config/codeql/config`; `/dev/null`, or a link to it, means none. If it
exists, the wrapper writes the consumer's lines and then its own to
`codeql-config-<uid>-<sha256>` under `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` when it is a writable
directory, else `TMPDIR`, else `/tmp`, and execs `codeql`. The name comes from
the content, so the file outlives the wrapper and a `codeql` that codeql starts
reads it too. Each run writes it again and renames it into place over any file
of that name.

A consumer file that sets an option this wrapper owns (`--additional-packs`,
`--model-packs`, or `--search-path`, when configured) exits 2 with a message.
The wrapper adds lines and does not join option values, and CodeQL keeps one
value per option, so the added lines would silently drop one side's packs. The
one file used as it is holds every line of the wrapper's config and sets those
options with no other line: the merged file that a `codeql` this wrapper started
reads, such as a build command's. Any other line setting an owned option, beside
those lines too, is refused.

### Precompilation

A query spec's realization writes its qlpack.yml, with the language's library
dependency (`codeql/<language>-all: "*"` for bundled languages), over `src`,
then runs `codeql pack create`. That needs no network: dependencies resolve from
the engine's bundled packs. The output is the pack with `.qlx` plans, a lock
file and the libraries it uses under `.codeql/libraries`, about 11 MB for
javascript. In CI the two-query fixture compiled in 66 s and the RequestForgery
query in 98 s.

A model spec's realization only writes its qlpack.yml (`extensionTargets`,
`dataExtensions: ["*.model.yml"]`). A directory given as it is stays uncompiled
and resolves the same way.

### The model check's kind

`codeql-model-pack-mutation` adds a `sinkModel` row
`["fakehttp", "Member[request].Argument[0]", "request-forgery"]`, and a second
pack the same row for `Member[fetchUrl]`. `RequestForgeryCustomizations.qll`
makes every `ModelOutput::sinkNode(_, "request-forgery")` a
`RequestForgery::Sink`, as the bundled `ext/axios.model.yml` does for axios. The
query selects `RequestForgery::Sink`. It finds nothing in the fixture without
the packs and exactly `request(...)` and `fetchUrl(...)` with them.

### Checks

`checks/codeql-customize.nix`; each check's comment lists its arms. All are
x86_64-linux only, and their `$out` holds text. `codeql-custom-query-pack`
covers the `.qlx` plans, resolution, the merge with a consumer config and its
refusals, and the engine's Node. `codeql-extra-packages` runs a program from
`extraPackages` as `database create --command`, which runs the customized codeql
again. `codeql-model-pack-mutation` checks the rows above, appending, and the
refusal of a consumer `--model-packs` line.

`codeql-pack-specs` builds no engine. At eval, a spec is no derivation, a query
spec realized by `codeql-javascript` and `codeql-full` is two derivations and a
model spec one, and `codeql-bare`, `codeql-full` without `language` and a spec
in the other kind's field throw. `tryEval` cannot read a message, so a probe
evaluates `lib/customization.nix` over a stand-in engine and greps each refusal.
